standard.title: Boire (Present Tense — Irregular Verb)
standard.explanation: The verb 'boire' (to drink) is an irregular verb in French. Its present-tense conjugation changes its stem from 'boi-' in first and second person (singular and plural) to 'buv-' in third person. This is called a stem-changing or boot verb. The conjugation is: je bois, tu bois, il/elle/on boit, nous buvons, vous buvez, ils/elles boivent. Pay attention to the spelling: 'bois' (I drink) sounds like 'bwa,' and 'nous buvons' uses the 'u' form. Example: 'Je bois du café.' (I drink coffee.)

examples.french: Il boit du jus de fruit.

advanced.title: Boire — Full Conjugation, Common Expressions & Partitive Article
advanced.explanation: The verb 'boire' (to drink) is an irregular boot verb with two distinct stems: 'boi-' (je bois, tu bois, il/elle/on boit, ils/elles boivent) and 'buv-' (nous buvons, vous buvez). The partitive article (du, de la, de l', des) is frequently used with 'boire' to express quantity or type of beverage: 'je bois du café' (I drink coffee), 'elle boit de la limonade' (she drinks lemonade). Common expressions with 'boire' include: 'boire un verre' (to have a drink), 'boire à la santé de quelqu'un' (to toast someone), 'avoir soif et boire' (to be thirsty and drink). The passé composé of 'boire' is 'j'ai bu' (I drank).
